name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Turkish lira passed 50 per dollar on 3 Nov in managed depreciation; no major EM default, capital controls or IMF rescue
state: The Turkish lira breached 50 per US dollar for the first time on 3 Nov after annual inflation rose to 29.8% in October (Shafaq News); it has weakened gradually rather than falling 10% in a month. Searches on 13 Nov found no major emerging economy in default, imposing capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support.
for_you: Higher US rates and a firm dollar tend to raise borrowing costs for emerging economies and weaken their currencies. Travellers, importers and investors with exposure to Turkey and other high-inflation markets face currency losses and price rises.
rubric_hit: Normal: no major EM currency down >10% in a month, no emergency IMF request, default or capital controls

sources.title: Shafaq News — Turkish lira breaches 50 per dollar to record low

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
